steps.u: Compute the average fuel use per 100 km per vehicle model for October from the trips table, excluding trips under 5 km. BigQuery.

steps.r: vehicle_id STRING, model STRING, km FLOAT, litres FLOAT, started_at TIMESTAMP

i.content:
SELECT model, SUM(litres) / SUM(km) * 100 AS l_per_100km, COUNT(*) AS trips
FROM `fleet.trips`
WHERE km >= 5 AND started_at >= '2026-10-01' AND started_at < '2026-11-01'
GROUP BY model ORDER BY l_per_100km

steps.r:
model | l_per_100km | trips
Van-A | 9.1 | 1840
Truck-B | 24.7 | 612
Van-C | 8.8 | 77

steps.a: I weighted by distance (total litres over total km) rather than averaging each trip's ratio, so a long trip counts more than a short one. Van-C has only 77 trips, so its figure is less reliable.

reference.summary: Wrote a BigQuery query for October fuel use per 100 km by vehicle model, excluding trips under 5 km, and ran it. It divides total litres by total distance rather than averaging per-trip ratios; one model has only 77 trips, so its figure is less reliable.
